clue.text: Far-sighted king, an old poet in cloistered surroundings

indicators.note: the cloistered word forms surroundings that the king and the poet sit inside

parts.note: pent means shut in or confined, as in a cloister
R is short for rex, Latin for king
Ovid was a Roman poet of the Augustan age

explanation.surface: A visionary monarch and a classical poet are pictured together in a monastery's cloisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; 'surroundings' is what tells you the confining word wraps round the king and the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone provident plans ahead for future needs, which is being far-sighted in the prudent sense.

clue.text: "Dad's Army" goes down well in Italy

parts.note: Dad is Pa, so Dad's is Pa's
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: The British TV sitcom Dad's Army is said to be popular with Italian viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army was a much-loved British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard; here it is just PA'S plus TA (Territorial Army).
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is the staple Italian food, something eaten, i.e. going down, with relish in Italy.

clue.text: Played in a sorrowful manner, before heading off for a drink

indicators.note: with its heading off, the musical term loses its opening letter

parts.note: doloroso is the musical direction to play sorrowfully

explanation.surface: A musician plays mournfully, then leaves for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, rich style of sherry, a fortified wine drink.

clue.text: A bit of a Greek character

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, as in not one jot
the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a very small quantity and a letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Art supporter's never-ending relaxation

indicators.note: never-ending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an easel supports a painting while it is made

explanation.surface: A patron of the arts enjoys endless leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is a state of rest and comfort, a synonym of relaxation.

clue.text: The nicest society can show irritability

indicators.note: the letters can show something else when rearranged, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: Even the most refined social circle can display bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can show' rearranges THE NICEST into TETCHINE, the start of the answer, and S finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchiness is peevish bad temper, a synonym of irritability.

clue.text: Let this off to vent anger

definitions.text: Let this off to vent anger

parts.words: Let this off to vent anger
parts.note: the idiom of releasing pent-up pressure, as a boiler does, used for releasing pent-up rage

explanation.definitionFit: To let off steam is the idiom for releasing anger or energy, from boilers venting vapour.

clue.text: The highlight of a leap year?

definitions.text: The highlight of a leap year?

parts.words: The highlight of a leap year?
parts.note: reads as the best part of a year with 29 February, but means the season when things leap up, like lambs and shoots

explanation.definitionFit: Spring is the season of growth and bounding lambs, so the word also suggests a time for leaping.

clue.text: Essential part in a golfer's equipment, when going up for the title

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golfer places the ball on
the pith is the core or essence of something

explanation.surface: A key component of a golfer's kit rises in importance when a championship title is at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when going up' works because this is a down entry, read upwards; the core part then sits inside the turned-round golf peg.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive name or title, such as 'the Great' after a king's name.

clue.text: Art Room A1 used for temporary suspensions

indicators.note: the letters are used to build something new, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A first-rate art room is set aside for pauses in activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges ART ROOM A I (the 1 standing for I); 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria is the plural of moratorium, an officially agreed temporary halt or suspension.

clue.text: Terrible cost, this, to register a dog

indicators.note: something terrible is mangled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a terrier is a register or roll of landed property

explanation.surface: It costs an awful lot to get a dog licensed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges COST THIS into SCOTTISH. The less familiar sense of terrier, a register of land holdings, supplies the rest; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish terrier, or Scottie, is a short-legged breed of dog.

clue.text: Star making a comeback associated with the bard

indicators.note: coming back means the word runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness

explanation.surface: A star actor returns to perform Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare, the Bard, was born at Stratford-upon-Avon and is called the Bard of Avon.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Avon is tied to Shakespeare through the title Bard of Avon.

clue.text: The songbird in question to move very slowly

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: what is a question word
to inch is to creep forward bit by bit

explanation.surface: The bird being discussed seems to be creeping along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in question' reads as 'under discussion', but 'in' is the container signal splitting the two pieces apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The whinchat is a small European songbird of the thrush family.

clue.text: Perhaps "The Good Pub Guide" gives report of superior place for drink

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: best cellar, the finest place for storing wine

explanation.surface: A guide to good pubs is a fine source for where to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' is a link. The Good Pub Guide is a popular British annual guidebook to pubs, so it is an example of a big seller.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular guidebook that sells in large numbers is an example of a top-selling book.

clue.text: Rule symbolically expressed about English motor racing

parts.note: a formula is a rule written in symbols, as in maths or chemistry
on means about, as in a talk on a topic

explanation.surface: A rule written in symbols concerns English motorsport.
explanation.definitionFit: Formula One is the top class of single-seater motor racing championships.

clue.text: Ruined, sad and was affection by emotions

parts.note: broke means penniless, financially ruined
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Bankrupt and depressed, someone was overcome by feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published has 'affection', plainly a slip for 'affected'; the definition reads 'was affected by emotions'. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To break down is to lose control and weep, overcome by strong feeling.

clue.text: Order examples for the works?

parts.note: to book is to order or reserve in advance
cases are instances or examples

explanation.surface: Someone orders samples for a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the works' suggests a factory, but here means literary works, the books a bookcase holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookcases are furniture made to hold written works, so they exist for books.

clue.text: Coach out for a trip in Turkey

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the word is tripped up and its letters jumble

explanation.surface: A coach heads out on an excursion in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a trip' jumbles the word out, giving UTO. 'Coach' tempts as a bus for the trip; it is a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor coaches a student privately, so coach is a synonym.

clue.text: Start the attack

definitions.meaning: a beginning, as of an illness

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a beginning and an assault, the forward rush of an enemy.

clue.text: Pictures within range of the old city

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a span is the full range or extent of something
art means pictures and paintings collectively

explanation.surface: Paintings are found throughout the ancient city's area.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan describes things belonging to Sparta, the ancient Greek city-state.

clue.text: Animal doctor nearly gets degree about ways to communicate

indicators.note: the degree goes about, i.e. around, the rest

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

explanation.surface: A vet almost earns a qualification in communications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal doctor' looks like VET but splits into two separate pieces; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The mass media are the press, radio and television, channels for communicating to the public.

clue.text: Girl on date, her boa loosely flung round

indicators.note: flung around loosely, the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman on a date has her feather boa draped about her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely flung round' rearranges HER BOA into EBORAH; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Deborah is a girl's name, a given name as an example of 'girl'.

clue.text: One for raising arch that's slender and with wings

parts.note: a crane is a machine for lifting loads
fly is slang for sharp or knowing, as is arch

explanation.surface: A lifting machine raises a slim, winged arch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' suggests a curved structure, but it is the adjective meaning knowing, slangily FLY. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly, or daddy-long-legs, is a slender winged insect with long legs.

clue.text: Murder victim — a lady losing her head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter goes

parts.note: Mabel is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman is beheaded in a murder.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Abel was killed by his brother Cain, the first murder victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel is the Bible's first murder victim, slain by his brother Cain.

clue.text: The composer to hear, they say

indicators.note: what they say is heard, so the word is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: list is an old word meaning to listen or hear

explanation.surface: People talk about hearing the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso of the Romantic era.

clue.text: Passage with one tenor holding a note

indicators.note: holding means the outer pair contains the other pieces

parts.note: T is short for tenor in choral music
D is a musical note
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In a passage of music, a solo tenor sustains a note.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are loosely ordered: A and T hold D and I. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage leading into a mine.

clue.text: Top one in a million? No, the reverse

indicators.note: the preceding 'in' is overturned: instead of one inside the other, the reverse holds

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
M is an abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Something is the best, one in a million, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in a million' would put ACE inside M; 'No, the reverse' puts M inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the peak or highest point, so it means the top.

clue.text: After collapsing, do stores etc sell to repay debts?

indicators.note: collapsed, the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: When a business goes under, do the shops hold a sale to pay off their creditors?
explanation.walkthrough: 'After collapsing' rearranges DO STORES ETC SELL. The definition is playful: the idiom means taking revenge, paying back old wrongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling old scores means getting even for past wrongs, cryptically repaying debts of injury.

clue.text: Detector of meson, a research tool

indicators.note: the letters come out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A device for detecting mesons is a useful tool in research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tool' is a link continuing the definition's surface; the answer runs across meSON A Research.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar detects underwater objects by sending out sound pulses and timing echoes.

clue.text: Beg outside church? Could be for the high jump

definitions.text: Could be for the high jump

indicators.note: one word goes outside the other

parts.note: to entreat is to beg earnestly

explanation.surface: Someone pleads outside church, perhaps facing severe punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the high jump' means in trouble in British idiom, but here it is literal: a ballet leap.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet leap in which the dancer crosses the feet repeatedly in the air.
